title: Smudge — 18mo fancy rat: chattering breathing and red-stained eyes
presentation: 18-month-old male fancy rat, six weeks of noisy breathing that the owner describes as chattering. Red-brown staining around both eyes and nose. One cage mate has started sneezing.

stages.title: Read the presentation
stages.briefing: Weight 480 g, BCS 4/9. Audible upper-airway rattle, RR 100/min with mild abdominal effort. Red-brown crusting at both medial canthi and the nares. Lung auscultation: harsh sounds bilaterally, no clear crackles. No cyanosis. Kept on wood-shaving bedding in a room where the household smokes. Temperature 37.9°C.

options.label: Red-brown staining at the canthi and nares
options.detail: Porphyrin, not blood — a stress and illness marker in rats

options.label: Six weeks of progressive upper-airway noise
options.detail: A chronic course, not an acute event

options.label: A cage mate with the same signs
options.detail: Points to something transmissible in the colony

options.label: Wood-shaving bedding and household smoke
options.detail: Genuine irritants, but they do not spread between cages

options.label: Temperature 37.9°C
options.detail: Within the normal range for a rat

stages.explanation: Porphyrin staining is the sign most often misread as blood, and it reliably marks a rat that is unwell rather than injured. Two rats in one cage with the same six-week course puts an infectious agent at the top of the list, while the irritants stay on it as aggravating factors. Recognising which findings travel between animals is how a single-patient consultation becomes a colony plan.

stages.title: Choose the diagnostics
stages.briefing: The owner has four rats and wants to know what is wrong and what to do about the others.

options.label: Deep nasal or tracheal swab for Mycoplasma pulmonis PCR
options.detail: Names the agent the colony is sharing

options.label: Bacterial culture and sensitivity from the same site
options.detail: Secondary invaders decide the antibiotic

options.label: Thoracic radiographs under light sedation
options.detail: Grades the lower-airway damage

options.label: Cytology of the airway sample
options.detail: Neutrophils, bacteria, ciliated cell damage

options.label: Full haematology and biochemistry
options.detail: Chronic disease and organ screening before treatment

options.label: Blood culture
options.detail: Septicaemia is not the picture in a rat that has been eating for six weeks

options.label: Allergen-specific IgE serology
options.detail: Not a validated approach in rats, and it would not change the plan

stages.explanation: The point of the PCR is that it changes what you tell the owner about the other three rats — M. pulmonis is endemic in pet rats and eradication is not on the table, so the conversation becomes control, husbandry and expectations. Culture with sensitivity is what gets the antibiotic right, because the secondary bacteria, not the mycoplasma, are what respond quickly.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: M. pulmonis PCR positive on tracheal swab. Culture: Pasteurella pneumotropica, sensitive to doxycycline and enrofloxacin. Cytology: neutrophilic inflammation with intracellular bacteria. Radiographs: peribronchial cuffing with patchy alveolar pattern in the caudodorsal lung fields, no consolidated abscess. Haematology: mild neutrophilia. Biochemistry unremarkable.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do the results support?

options.label: Chronic mycoplasmal respiratory disease with secondary bacterial infection
options.detail: PCR positive plus a cultured invader and neutrophils

options.label: The cage mates are already exposed and should be managed as a group
options.detail: M. pulmonis spreads readily and is usually colony-wide

options.label: Antibiotic choice should follow the sensitivity result
options.detail: Doxycycline covers both the mycoplasma and the isolate

options.label: Radiographs show a pulmonary abscess needing surgery
options.detail: Cuffing and patchy alveolar change, no discrete abscess

options.label: The bedding and smoke are the primary cause
options.detail: They aggravate; the PCR names the primary agent

stages.explanation: This is a two-agent disease: the mycoplasma strips the ciliated defences and the opportunist does the visible damage, which is why the treatment has to cover both and why the response is partial rather than curative. Reading the radiographs as an abscess would send the rat to surgery for a lesion that is diffuse inflammation. The irritants are still worth removing — they are just not the reason two rats are ill.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: M. pulmonis PCR positive, Pasteurella pneumotropica cultured, neutrophilic airway cytology, peribronchial cuffing on radiographs, one affected cage mate.

options.label: Chronic respiratory disease of rats — M. pulmonis with secondary bacterial bronchopneumonia
options.detail: Both agents, and the chronicity, in one line

options.label: Primary bacterial pneumonia
options.detail: Understates the mycoplasma that made it possible

options.label: Allergic airway disease from bedding and smoke
options.detail: Does not explain a positive PCR shared with a cage mate

options.label: Pulmonary neoplasia
options.detail: Wrong age, wrong radiographic pattern, and it would not spread

options.label: Aspiration pneumonia
options.detail: No history of a dysphagic or regurgitating rat

stages.explanation: Calling it chronic respiratory disease sets honest expectations: doxycycline with an anti-inflammatory will improve this rat, dust-free bedding and a smoke-free room will help all four, and none of it eliminates the organism. Owners who are told this at the start manage relapses far better than owners promised a cure.
